headline: Higgins views neo-clouds as the purest way to play AI compute demand and prefers them over hyperscalers for thematic exposure
reasoning: Higgins explains neo-clouds are businesses that build compute capacity, layer software and infrastructure on top, and rent that capacity to AI labs and enterprises — similar to hyperscalers but more pure-play. The big three hyperscalers (Microsoft Azure, Amazon AWS, Google Cloud) are rental businesses that originated from software, whereas neo-clouds are built from the ground up for this purpose. With around 20 names on Nasdaq, half a dozen well-known, Higgins sees the neo-cloud cohort as a superior vehicle for expressing the AI demand thematic compared to large diversified hyperscalers.
quote: Neo clouds are effectively similar leverage. So the neo clouds, um, that are listed, majority of them having been listed on the Nasdaq. They're effectively businesses that that go and build capacity. They look to then fill that capacity via a software and an infrastructure layer, and then push that capacity out to either the AI labs or to effectively enterprises and anybody that wishes to use compute. So the neo clouds in our view, are more pure play way to access compute and access where where the cloud market is going. And so as a result, you know, they're really a pure play form of of really trading making that AI trade.
